# Design research document map


<!-- Generated by _scripts/build_design_research_map.py. Edit document-map-relations.json for conceptual relationships. -->

The map covers the published design-research collection. The [index]({{< ref "ai/design-research/00-index" >}}) gives descriptions and a reading order. The reassembly log records original text movements and preservation checks.

Conceptual arrows show suggested relationships between discussions. They do not establish mathematical dependencies, causal relations, an accepted architecture, or a required research sequence. Original dialogues and sibling comments remain separate.

The snapshot includes 72 content notes, 32 sibling comment notes, and 3 navigation or audit files. Private external-source records are omitted from this public edition.

## How to use the map


First, use the topic diagrams to choose a discussion. Second, use the catalogue to follow explicit links and read the sibling comments. Third, use the conceptual relationship table to inspect the reason for each arrow.

The IDs identify files. O means overview, F means foundations, C means collaboration, L means language, I means investigation, R means runtime, E means reports and evaluation, and S means source material. A final C identifies a sibling comments file.

| Relationship | Meaning | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Conceptual | A suggested relation between the content of two discussions. | A checked passage and its current line number. |
| Explicit link | One document links to another file. | The original link location, stored in the data snapshot. |
| Comments on | A comments file has a matching sibling note. | The current file paths. |
| Audit reference | A link concerns the movement log or another audit file. | The recorded link. Historical checks have not been rerun by the map builder. |

## Conceptual coverage


The relationship table connects 71 of 72 content notes through 81 authored relationships. The 11 topic diagrams show 59 content notes. Coverage describes navigation, not completeness of the research or strength of its evidence.

Catalogue entries without conceptual arrows: [O03]({{< ref "ai/design-research/00-overview/03-original-index-notes" >}}). Their explicit links remain in the catalogue and data snapshot.

The sibling [map comments]({{< ref "ai/design-research/document-map-comments" >}}) explain the reviewed gaps, the historical index, and the remaining work. The comments are separate editorial analysis and are excluded from relationship extraction.

## Boundaries and open choices


The map retains the distinctions below. Grouping discussions does not resolve their differences.

| Discussions | Distinction to retain |
|---|---|
| [F01]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/01-constrained-generativity" >}}), [F08]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/08-semantic-substrate-builder-method" >}}), [F04]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/04-participant-neutral-system-model" >}}), [O06]({{< ref "ai/design-research/00-overview/06-research-scope-and-hierarchy" >}}) | The general principle, builder method, and participant-neutral architecture are different levels. A database, shared state, or DSL is not a universal requirement. |
| [L02]({{< ref "ai/design-research/03-language-and-compiler/02-typed-dsl-and-compiler" >}}), [F09]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/09-verification-and-acceptance" >}}), [I03]({{< ref "ai/design-research/04-investigation-and-epistemics/03-epistemic-contracts-for-rag" >}}) | Compiler validity, operator correctness, evidence support, and acceptance for a purpose require different checks. |
| [F09]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/09-verification-and-acceptance" >}}), [R05]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/05-trusted-effect-boundaries" >}}), [L13]({{< ref "ai/design-research/03-language-and-compiler/13-domain-semantics-and-operation-contracts" >}}) | A described operation or accepted result does not establish authority for an external action. |
| [L03]({{< ref "ai/design-research/03-language-and-compiler/03-declarative-programming-model" >}}), [L11]({{< ref "ai/design-research/03-language-and-compiler/11-behavioral-compilation-and-specification" >}}), [GUIDE-C]({{< ref "ai/design-research/00-index-comments" >}}) | Maintained declarations and generated executable behavior might be layers or alternatives. The notes do not select the relationship. |
| [I04]({{< ref "ai/design-research/04-investigation-and-epistemics/04-provenance-and-argumentation-foundations" >}}), [I06]({{< ref "ai/design-research/04-investigation-and-epistemics/06-bounded-corpus-evidence-synthesis" >}}), [I03]({{< ref "ai/design-research/04-investigation-and-epistemics/03-epistemic-contracts-for-rag" >}}) | Lineage, corpus consideration, retrieval recall, evidence support, and conflict resolution are distinct properties. |
| [R06]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/06-program-versions-runs-and-results" >}}), [R09]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/09-declarative-system-configuration-and-instantiation" >}}), [R10]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/10-configuration-publishing-and-version-identity" >}}), [R11]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/11-evaluation-plans-and-system-configuration" >}}) | A program revision, resolved system revision, environment binding, evaluation plan, and observed run are different records. |
| [R01]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/01-generalized-agent-runtime" >}}), [R06]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/06-program-versions-runs-and-results" >}}), [R09]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/09-declarative-system-configuration-and-instantiation" >}}) | Using recorded observations differs from making new live model or tool calls. Matching configuration identity does not guarantee exact outcomes. |
| [C02]({{< ref "ai/design-research/02-human-ai-collaboration/02-sensemaking-and-epistemic-action" >}}), [E11]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/11-human-ai-collaboration-evaluation" >}}), [E05]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/05-agent-runtime-evaluation-and-benchmarks" >}}), [E07]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/07-investigation-evaluation-and-benchmarks" >}}), [E08]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/08-behavioral-compilation-evaluation-and-failure-modes" >}}) | Human understanding, runtime enforcement, evidence quality, and program generalization need different tests. |
| [F10]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/10-complexity-and-work-structure" >}}), [E09]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/09-long-running-work-failures-and-field-study" >}}), [E05]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/05-agent-runtime-evaluation-and-benchmarks" >}}) | The work profile is proposed, the field study has not been conducted, and injected failures do not validate every task dimension. |
| [F12]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/12-research-terms-and-levels-of-analysis" >}}), [F11]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/11-participant-profiles-and-work-allocation" >}}), [O08]({{< ref "ai/design-research/00-overview/08-collaborative-computation-and-alice-research-scope" >}}), [E12]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/12-multiagent-coordination-and-system-semantics" >}}) | Working cognitive definitions, assigned work roles, security authority, and the emergence of agency are not interchangeable. |
| [O08]({{< ref "ai/design-research/00-overview/08-collaborative-computation-and-alice-research-scope" >}}), [O06]({{< ref "ai/design-research/00-overview/06-research-scope-and-hierarchy" >}}), [E13]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/13-research-method-and-claim-validation" >}}) | Alice is a separate research direction. Sharing a method does not make one direction a prerequisite of the other. |
| [R11]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/11-evaluation-plans-and-system-configuration" >}}), [E13]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/13-research-method-and-claim-validation" >}}), [E11]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/11-human-ai-collaboration-evaluation" >}}) | A runnable evaluation configuration is not evidence that its scoring rules are valid or its illustrative threshold is justified. |
| [F03]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/03-behavioral-types-and-protocols" >}}), [R04]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/04-formal-models-for-agent-execution" >}}), [C05]({{< ref "ai/design-research/02-human-ai-collaboration/05-joint-activity-and-collaboration-model" >}}), [F09]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/09-verification-and-acceptance" >}}) | Permitted interaction sequences, safety, eventual completion, shared understanding, and evidence truth require different checks. A monitor proposal does not establish all of them. |
| [L04]({{< ref "ai/design-research/03-language-and-compiler/04-dsl-as-mediation-layer" >}}), [L05]({{< ref "ai/design-research/03-language-and-compiler/05-layered-design-model" >}}), [L02]({{< ref "ai/design-research/03-language-and-compiler/02-typed-dsl-and-compiler" >}}), [R05]({{< ref "ai/design-research/05-runtime-and-execution/05-trusted-effect-boundaries" >}}) | A more structured program or isolated runner does not by itself grant authority. The accepted representation, current permission, and confirmed external outcome remain separate. |
| [L01]({{< ref "ai/design-research/03-language-and-compiler/01-dsl-reliability" >}}), [L12]({{< ref "ai/design-research/03-language-and-compiler/12-tickloom-semantic-model-and-scenario-dsl" >}}), [L07]({{< ref "ai/design-research/03-language-and-compiler/07-semantic-kernel" >}}), [F09]({{< ref "ai/design-research/01-foundations/09-verification-and-acceptance" >}}) | The captured DSL examples illustrate domain vocabulary and scenario construction. They do not measure general generation reliability or establish every possible protocol execution. |
| [E10]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/10-interactive-investigation-position-paper" >}}), [C02]({{< ref "ai/design-research/02-human-ai-collaboration/02-sensemaking-and-epistemic-action" >}}), [E07]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/07-investigation-evaluation-and-benchmarks" >}}), [E11]({{< ref "ai/design-research/06-research-reports/11-human-ai-collaboration-evaluation" >}}) | Interactive correction, user understanding, retrieval quality, and contract enforcement need distinct observations. The proposed paper and studies are not completed research. |

## Sources and related local collections


The references below connect the collection to source redirects, retained contextual drafts, project examples, and the sibling interactive-systems collection. Only direct references are mapped. The source and audit logs remain authoritative for original ranges; the map does not infer text origin from a link.

Private external-source paths and their metadata are omitted from this public edition.

## Data and maintenance


The [data snapshot](/ai/design-research/document-map.assets/document-map.json) contains every mapped file's hash, explicit outgoing and incoming relationships, link occurrences, sibling pairs, conceptual evidence, and navigation findings. Incoming relationships can be found by a relationship's `to` field. The [relationship definitions](/ai/design-research/document-map.assets/document-map-relations.json) contain the authored interpretations and diagram selections.

The map builder reads the notes without changing them. Check the saved map from the notes root:

```sh
python3 _scripts/build_design_research_map.py --check
```


After notes change, inspect updated output with `--emit markdown` and `--emit json`, then apply the output to the generated files with a patch. The checker reports stale output rather than rewriting notes. Update evidence passages when the meaning changes, not merely to make a check pass.

The generated map files, relationship definitions, and sibling map comments are excluded from the document inventory to avoid counting the map's own links as evidence. The data snapshot records the map comments separately by path and hash. The index link to the map is also excluded from relationship extraction.

Limits of the scan:

- External collections are boundary references, not a complete map of notes or source archive.
- Legacy wiki links are resolved only when a local path or unique filename identifies a file.
- Code, audit table paths in code spans, citations, and plain-text mentions are not document links.
- Inline links must stay on one line. Setext headings are not indexed; HTML a elements with id or name are indexed.
- Audit links show recorded history; they do not recheck prior byte-range reconstructions.
- Private external-source titles, headings, and hashes are omitted from the public map.
